mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW X5 35i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full BMW X5 35i engine replacement typically costs £2,800-£4,800 supply-only for rebuilt N55B30 units, or £4,500-£6,500 fitted by a specialist. N55B30 rebuilt supply-only: £3,800-£4,800 depending on mileage and condition. Used N55B30 engines: £1,200-£2,800. Professional fitting adds £800-£1,500 to any engine purchase.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW X5 35i N55 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N55 is generally more reliable than its twin-turbo predecessor, the N54. However, it has well-documented weak points: High-Pressure Fuel Pump (HPFP) failure is common between 50,000-80,000 miles, valve cover gasket leaks are frequent from 60,000 miles, and timing chain tensioner wear can occur on higher-mileage units. With proactive maintenance, the N55 is a durable and enjoyable engine.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of HPFP failure on a BMW X5 35i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs are long cranking times before the engine starts, rough idling, hesitation or stumbling under acceleration, loss of power, and the Check Engine Light illuminating. In extreme cases, the engine may stall while driving or fail to start at all. If you notice any of these symptoms on your X5 35i, have the HPFP inspected immediately.

mainEntity.name: Does the BMW X5 35i have timing chain problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N55 engine is not as prone to catastrophic timing chain failure as the N47 diesel, but timing chain tensioner wear is a known issue on higher-mileage units. Symptoms include a rattling or slapping noise from the engine, especially during cold start-up. If you hear this noise, have the tensioner inspected - replacement is far cheaper than a full engine rebuild.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a high-mileage BMW X5 35i?

acceptedAnswer.text: For an X5 35i (E70 or F15) worth £6,000-£18,000, a £2,800-£4,800 rebuilt N55 engine can make financial sense if the body, gearbox and interior are sound. The N55 is a well-supported engine with good parts availability. Always factor the 12-month warranty into your replacement decision - a rebuilt engine with warranty offers peace of mind that a high-mileage used unit cannot match.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the BMW X5 sDrive35i and xDrive35i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The sDrive35i is rear-wheel drive only (available on the F15 generation), while the xDrive35i is all-wheel drive. Both use the same N55B30 engine with the same power output (306hp). The drivetrain difference affects handling and fuel economy but does not change the engine itself. When ordering a replacement engine, the same N55B30 unit fits both sDrive and xDrive variants - though fitting labour may differ slightly due to drivetrain component access.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW X5 35i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW X5 35i was introduced with the E70 facelift in 2010, replacing the naturally aspirated 3.0-litre straight-six petrol engine. It was the first X5 petrol to feature BMW's N55 turbocharged inline-six - the brand's first six-cylinder engine to combine turbocharging, direct fuel injection and Valvetronic. The 35i continued into the F15 generation, available in both rear-wheel drive sDrive and all-wheel drive xDrive forms, until it was phased out in favour of the B58-powered 40i.

milestones.description: N55B30 introduced with E70 LCI (facelift), 3.0L turbocharged straight-six, 306hp, 8-speed automatic transmission
F15 generation launches; 35i continues with N55B30, now available as sDrive35i (RWD) and xDrive35i (AWD)
2018 - N55B30 remains the sole petrol six-cylinder option in the X5 35i, producing 306hp and 400Nm torque
F15 production ends; G05 generation replaces the 35i with the B58-powered 40i

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW X5 35i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points - from the E70 launch to the final F15 examples.

commonProblems.h2: BMW X5 35i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW X5 35i is powered by the N55 turbocharged straight-six petrol engine - BMW's first turbocharged six-cylinder to combine forced induction with direct injection and Valvetronic. While the N55 is generally more reliable than its predecessor (the twin-turbo N54), it has well-documented weak points that can lead to expensive repairs. Below we break down the most common N55 failures on the X5 35i, what you'll pay at a dealer versus a specialist, and when replacement is the only sensible answer. Every rebuilt N55 engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: High-Pressure Fuel Pump (HPFP) Failure - Why the BMW X5 35i N55 Engine Stalls or Won't Start
problems.rootCause: The High-Pressure Fuel Pump is a known weak point on the N55 engine. A failing HPFP can lead to hard starting, long cranking times, engine stalling, loss of power, and in some cases, the engine may not start at all. Fuel pump failure can cause an engine stall while driving, increasing the risk of a crash.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace high-pressure fuel pump with rebuilt or OEM unit, fuel system flush
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; prevents stalling and further damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt N55B30 with new HPFP and upgraded components, bench tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if HPFP failure caused injector or engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW X5 35i (E70 or F15) in fair condition is worth £6,000-£18,000 depending on age, mileage and specification. An HPFP replacement at specialist rates (£550-£1,000) is excellent value on any X5 35i worth over £6,000. If the engine has suffered internal damage from fuel starvation, evaluate the cost of a full rebuild against the vehicle's value - for a well-maintained example, a rebuilt N55 with warranty is a sound investment.
problems.recommendation: HPFP failure on the N55 gives clear warning signs - long cranking, rough idle, and hesitation under load. Address it immediately. A specialist HPFP replacement costs under £1,000 and prevents the pump from failing completely and leaving you stranded. On any X5 35i approaching 60,000 miles, consider preventative HPFP inspection or replacement - it's cheaper than a tow truck and a full engine rebuild.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N55B30 BMW X5 35i engine prices

problems.h4: Valve Cover Gasket Leaks - Why BMW X5 35i Engines Smell of Burning Oil
problems.rootCause: The valve cover gasket in the N55 engine is prone to leaking over time. A leaking gasket allows oil to seep onto the hot engine block or exhaust manifold, creating a burning oil smell and visible oil leaks around the engine bay. If left unaddressed, oil can reach the spark plugs and cause misfires.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove valve cover, replace gasket, clean oil residue, refit
repairOptions.longevity: Viable at first sign of oil leak or burning smell

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt N55B30 with new gaskets and seals, bench tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil leak caused misfire damage or if engine has other major issues

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For an X5 35i worth £6,000-£18,000, a £350-£700 specialist valve cover gasket replacement is straightforward and cost-effective. This is a maintenance item, not a catastrophic failure - addressing it promptly preserves the engine and prevents more expensive repairs.
problems.recommendation: The valve cover gasket is a known wear item on the N55. If you notice a burning oil smell after parking or see oil residue around the top of the engine, have the gasket replaced at your next service. At specialist rates, this is one of the most cost-effective repairs you can do on a high-mileage X5 35i. Don't ignore it - oil leaks can lead to misfires and, in extreme cases, engine fires.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for N55B30 valve cover gasket repair for BMW X5 35i

problems.h4: Timing Chain & VANOS Issues - Why BMW X5 35i Engines Rattle on Start-Up
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner can wear over time, allowing the timing chain to stretch or slacken. This produces a rattling noise from the engine, especially during cold start-up. If not addressed, the chain can skip teeth or fail completely, causing catastrophic engine damage. VANOS solenoid failure is also common, triggering codes 2D54, 2D55 and 2C58.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain tensioner only, no chain replacement
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early with rattle but no chain stretch

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, guides, tensioner and VANOS solenoids
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has stretched or VANOS codes are present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt N55B30 with new timing components, bench tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has snapped or caused valve/piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For an X5 35i worth £6,000-£18,000, a timing chain tensioner replacement at specialist rates (£350-£600) is excellent preventative maintenance. If the chain has stretched and requires full replacement (£1,200-£2,000), this is still justifiable on a car worth over £8,000. If the chain has snapped, evaluate the cost of a full rebuilt engine against the vehicle's value - for a well-maintained F15 X5 35i, a rebuilt N55 with warranty is often the right call.
problems.recommendation: The N55 timing chain is not as prone to catastrophic failure as the N47 diesel, but tensioner wear is real. If you hear a rattling noise on cold start that disappears as the engine warms, act immediately - a £350 tensioner replacement saves thousands. Once the chain snaps, the engine is beyond economic repair. On any X5 35i approaching 80,000 miles, have the timing chain tensioner inspected.
